title: Add FakeTensor, ProxyTensor and serialization support to inductor_compiled_code HOP
body:
My local tweaks of https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/172274

I ended up making a small e2e test for "non-strict trace on full model, with torch.compile on an inner transformer block", and made a few extra changes:

(1) my test also includes a buffer mutation, so I had to make sure that `auto_functionalize` supports outer non-strict trace

(2) In Ed's original PR, he tweaked the `inductor_compiled_code` HOP to stash the FX graph, so it can support fake tensor prop. This didn't play well with serialization, so I ended up stashing the FakeTensor outputs of the region on the HOP instead (this should also make tracing the `inductor_compiled_code` HOP much cheaper).

This won't actually quite work if any of the outputs are dynamic shapes, since you need to do some extra work to map input symbolic shapes to their outputs when doing fake prop, which I didn't implement, so I just error if any outputs of the inductor region have dynamic shapes for now (for flex they do not).

Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #174504

items.author: bdhirsh
items.body:
The main change I made compared to https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/172274 was that I had the inductor HOP stash the `fake_outputs` to do fake tensor prop with, instead of stashing the entire original FX graph. Mostly because I ran into serializability issues trying to stash the FX graph.

This will have problems if the outputs to each subgraph have dynamic shapes though.
items.diff_hunk:
@@ -616,6 +617,11 @@ def __init__(
         # This is set at compile time to avoid runtime overhead
         self._wrap_compiled_regions = config.wrap_inductor_compiled_regions
 
+        if self._wrap_compiled_regions:
+            self.fake_outputs = tuple(
+                [x.meta["val"] for x in gm.graph.find_nodes(op="output")[0].args[0]]
+            )

items.author: bdhirsh
items.body: I added a big e2e test that exercises hierarchical compile, and also mutates a global buffer so that auto_functionalize kicks in, That required this boxed calling convention change.
items.diff_hunk:
@@ -614,6 +614,9 @@ def __call__(self, *args, **kwargs):
         # Inlining has the benefit of allowing easiser fusion inside subgraph.
         # Though the epilogue graph contains copy_, it is OK because inductor can handle it
         # and this is also how we have been supporting top-level graph input mutation.
+        # Handle boxed calling convention
+        if getattr(self.orig_callable, "_boxed_call", False):
+            return tuple(torch.func.functionalize(self.orig_callable)(list(args)))
